document_summary: Official Boston.gov page describing the Housing Stability Notification Act (Boston Ordinance Sec. 10-11.7), which requires landlords to give tenants a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources and notify the City when ending a tenancy in Boston, MA.

rules.title: [notice-only] Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: Any landlord planning to end a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the notice to quit or notice of non-renewal, and must submit the notice and tenant contact information to the City through an online portal.
rules.key_value: Notice-of-rights requirement only; no just-cause protection
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords (and foreclosing owners for the City submission) planning to end a tenancy agreement in Boston.
rules.interaction: Notice-only ordinance that does not limit the grounds for eviction or non-renewal; a violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act requires
ALL LANDLORDS
planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
rules.conflict_note: Notice-of-rights ordinance only; it provides no just-cause protection and should not be read as limiting grounds for eviction.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date not stated in this page (the page calls the act 'new' but gives no date), so effective_date is null. Enforcement: warning for the 1st offense, $300 per day for later offenses; a violation does not halt the eviction. Source is an official city summary page, not the ordinance text.
